Sessions are Shared or Private; owners grant viewer access.

sources.finding: Enterprise only. Organization Usage shows per-user and per-model usage with CSV export; My Usage shows model and daily breakdowns. sources.title: Configuring Cosmos
sources.locator: Quickstart; Connect GitHub/Slack/Linear; Understanding your options; Choose a Starting Environment; Add Repositories; Pick Your Experts
sources.finding: Onboarding connects the Augment GitHub App (admin picks repos), optional Slack and Linear. Self-hosted is one command on a laptop, VM or server; Cloud hosts the VM from a base image (Ubuntu 24.04 default, TypeScript, Go, PHP, Ruby, Rust images) or your own. sources.title: Self-Hosted Daemon Overview
sources.finding: Install Auggie daemon release with npm, log in and run auggie daemon from the workspace; pools group hosts. sources.title: Ticket Manager: from ticket to PR
sources.locator: From ticket to PR; Connect your tools; Try it in your ticket tracker
sources.finding: Ticket Manager checks a delegated GitHub Issues, Linear or Jira ticket, asks PR Author to implement it, keeps the ticket updated and links the PR or MR back; humans review and merge. Code hosts: GitHub, GitLab Cloud, Azure DevOps Services, Bitbucket via custom setup. GitHub/Jira delegate by label (removed after the issue is claimed); Linear by delegating to the Cosmos agent.

sources.locator: About auggie cloud; API first; Declarative bundles; GitOps workflows

Experts, environments, MCP servers and residents are YAML bundles with init/export/validate/diff/apply; each apply creates an immutable version. Examples: session create, trigger disable, usage. Service-account tokens authenticate CI.

sources.finding: Team and Enterprise tenant admins create service accounts with non-expiring API tokens (session.json); deleting a token or account is permanent and disrupts automations using it.

sources.finding: Context Engine is exposed over MCP locally (Auggie as stdio server, real-time working-directory index) or remotely over HTTP (selected repos' default branches via GitHub App), with OAuth or API key auth; it offers codebase-retrieval to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Zed and others. Queries bill at token pricing plus the 40% fee.

sources.title: Auggie SDK
sources.finding: TypeScript (@augmentcode/auggie-sdk) and Python (auggie-sdk) SDKs with session-file, env-var or apiKey auth and custom tools.

sources.title: Self-Hosted Daemon Pools
sources.finding: Pools route sessions to an eligible daemon by workspace requirements and current load; isolated (git worktree) or shared workspace modes; pool bundles are a Preview CLI feature.

sources.title: Configuring Triggers
sources.locator: Trigger Types; Adding a Trigger; Event Type Reference; Payload Filters
sources.finding: Triggers open a session with the event payload: first-party GitHub, Linear, Slack, GitLab and PagerDuty (Cosmos owns upstream registration), cron schedules, and custom HTTPS webhooks. JSONLogic filters, optional max runs per minute, and Run sessions as the creator or a service account.

sources.title: Plugins and Marketplaces
sources.finding: Plugins bundle custom commands, subagents, hooks, skills and MCP servers, distributed through Git-repository marketplaces and enabled per user, project or local settings file.

sources.title: Rules
sources.locator: Rule locations; User vs Workspace; Frontmatter
sources.finding: Loads workspace .augment/rules, user ~/.augment/rules, AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) from the current and parent directories and .augment-guidelines; user rules always apply, workspace rules support always_apply, agent_requested and manual.

sources.title: Skills
sources.finding: Skills load from .augment/skills, .claude/skills or .agents/skills in the workspace or home directory.

sources.title: Tool Permissions
sources.locator: Intro; Permission Types and Precedence; Settings files; Allow/Block lists
sources.finding: toolPermissions rules (allow, deny, ask-user, webhook-policy, script-policy) are honored by Auggie CLI and Cosmos cloud agents but not the IDE extension; most restrictive wins; ask-user denies without a UI; managed settings at /etc/augment/settings.json; shell rules match by regex; unmatched tools follow implicit runtime behavior; a committed .augment/settings.json enforces policy on cloud agents.

sources.title: Subagents
sources.locator: Overview; Configuration fields; Tool restrictions; Supported models
sources.finding: Subagents run in parallel; built-in general-purpose, explore and plan agents; custom agents set model, thinking level and a tools allowlist or disabled_tools; codebase-retrieval searches the codebase.

sources.title: Ticket Dispatcher
sources.finding: Runs on a schedule, scans configured ticket sources, applies a readiness rubric, dispatches PR Author for ready tickets, respects a maximum of dispatcher-owned open changes and records skip reasons.

sources.title: Feedback Triager
sources.locator: Feedback Triager; Tickets and next steps
sources.finding: Each new top-level Slack message starts a session that claims the thread, classifies and investigates; it creates tickets in Linear, Jira or GitHub Issues automatically or on request after searching for duplicates, and never changes code itself.

sources.title: Using Schedules as Triggers
sources.locator: Adding a Schedule; Concurrency and Reliability
sources.finding: 5-field cron with IANA timezone. Each schedule runs in singleton mode: a fire that arrives while the previous run executes is skipped, not queued. Missed fires during pod transitions or leadership changes are not backfilled. Sessions run with the creator's permissions.

sources.title: Manage automations
sources.locator: Overview; Run History; Event History; Inspect events across automations
sources.finding: Automation pages show triggers with pause toggles, Run History with succeeded/failed counts for 24 hours and 7 days and each run's session (with its worker tree in the sidebar), Event History, and a cross-automation Event Log with payloads and headers.

sources.title: Managing Spaces
sources.finding: Sessions, Experts, environments, secrets and MCP servers belong to Spaces; a worker launched by a manager inherits the manager's Space so the worker subtree stays together. Any member can create a Space and becomes its owner; renaming, deleting and membership changes need an org admin or owner.

sources.title: Cosmos Experts
sources.locator: Overview; Sharing; What an Expert includes
sources.finding: Experts package system prompt, instructions, integrations, environment, model and worker Experts; shared privately, with teammates, a Space or the organization; Advisor can configure them.

sources.title: Expert templates
sources.finding: Templates include Cosmos Advisor, PR Author, PR Fixer, Risk Analyzer, Deep Reviewer, Pair Reviewer, Verifier, Incident Investigator, Feedback Triager, Project Builder, Ticket Manager, Ticket Dispatcher, Data Analyst, ROI Analyst and Code Review Memory.

sources.title: What's new in Auggie 1.x
sources.finding: Auggie 1.x prerelease adds /export to HTML or JSONL and /import to resume from JSONL, compaction, worktrees, a permissions manager and Notification hooks.

sources.title: CLI Reference
sources.finding: auggie --continue resumes the most recent session, --resume picks a saved session, --export converts a session JSONL to HTML.

sources.title: Migrate Code Review to Cosmos
sources.finding: The current Code Review bot on GitHub will be sunset; a guide moves reviews to Cosmos Deep Reviewer.

sources.title: Project Builder
sources.finding: Takes a large feature through design, architecture and ticket breakdown, then launches a PR Author worker per unit in dependency waves; never merges.

sources.title: Understanding Files
sources.locator: Scopes; Browsing; Versioning and Recovery; Limits
sources.finding: Files persist across sessions in User or Organization scope, sync at turn boundaries, show the agent that last wrote each file, and keep immutable attributed versions with time-decayed pruning; 1 MB per file, 100 MB per filesystem.

sources.title: Understanding Artifacts
sources.locator: About; Artifact types; Searching; Adding manually
sources.finding: Sessions store PR, Git branch, Linear issue (feature-flagged) and custom link artifacts; PRs opened through the GitHub tool attach automatically; Cmd+K finds sessions by PR, branch or Linear ID. Artifacts are per session.

sources.title: PR Fixer
sources.finding: Repairs review findings, CI failures and unambiguous merge conflicts on changes created without PR Author; never merges.

sources.title: Configure a code review pipeline
sources.finding: Risk Analyzer classifies each change and auto-approves intrinsically low-risk changes per org policy while routing higher-risk ones; Deep Reviewer reviews line by line; Pair Reviewer posts comments; cosmos approve evaluates a current-head approval policy (disabled by default) requiring no unresolved findings or comments.

sources.title: Okta Express Configuration
sources.finding: Okta JIT provisioning creates users on first login; Universal Logout lets Okta terminate sessions and tokens.

sources.title: Index your workspace
sources.finding: Opening a workspace uploads the codebase to Augment's cloud for indexing; .gitignore and .augmentignore control what is indexed.

sources.title: Daemon Configuration File
sources.finding: maxAgents caps concurrent child-agent sessions per daemon (default 100); allowIndexing defaults to false.

sources.title: Hooks
sources.finding: Hook timeout defaults to 60000 ms.

sources.title: Secrets Manager
sources.finding: Secrets are encrypted, write-only, stripped from logs and exported into the VM at boot only when the session is authorized, the secret applies to its Space and auto-install is on.

sources.title: augmentcode/auggie repository
sources.finding: The public repo at 8bd7186 holds docs, examples, a plugin marketplace, slash-command files and workflows under a custom proprietary license; the CLI and Cosmos source are not included.

sources.title: Auggie releases
sources.finding: v1.2.2 on 2026-11-17 and v1.3.0 prerelease builds several times a day from 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-20.

sources.title: What's new in Auggie 1.x
sources.finding: Auggie 1.x exports sessions as HTML or JSONL and resumes JSONL via /import; the page still labels 1.x prerelease.

sources.title: Managing Cosmos with auggie cloud
sources.finding: Experts, environments, MCP servers and residents use YAML bundles; export writes a remote resource locally and apply creates or updates it with an immutable version.

sources.title: Configure a code review pipeline
sources.locator: Deep Reviewer; Verifier; PR Dashboard Manager; cosmos approve
sources.finding: Per-PR Dashboard Manager summarizes Expert status, evidence, reviewed commits and actions. PR Fixer can repair Deep Reviewer findings. Disabled-by-default cosmos approve can require current-head review and no unaddressed Verifier defect against the current commit; approval never merges.

sources.title: Ticket Dispatcher
sources.finding: Ticket Dispatcher exposes backpressure limits and caps dispatcher-owned open changes to avoid flooding the review queue.

sources.title: Using Sessions
sources.finding: Shared sessions are readable by the organization; the owner may grant individual teammates viewer access. Conversation persists, but an environment paused for a long time may restart clean and lose uncommitted changes.

sources.title: Feedback Triager
sources.finding: Feedback Triager searches the configured tracker for plausible duplicates before filing; repeated requests reuse the existing result rather than repeating side effects.
